newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish Oct CPI seen buoying T-bill ylds at tender.
newsitem.headline: Polish Oct CPI seen buoying T-bill ylds at tender.

text.p: Polish October inflation data confirmed market expectations that interest rates would stay flat in the near-term, and analysts expected that would make investors bid for higher yields at Monday's primary tender.
The Central Statistical Office (GUS) said on Friday November prices rose 1.4 percent, which helped keep the year-on-year index flat at 19.5 percent from September.

The flat year-on-year index, a result of a change in the GUS basket of consumer goods at the start of the year, surprised the market because it had expected a drop to below 19 percent in line with earlier finance ministry forecasts.
"I think prices may fall one grosz on each maturity, as the market believes that base rates should not change in the mid-term," an analyst at a foreign investment company said.
"Investors would try to lift yields on Monday after October inflation proved the figure for the end of the year will not be any better than already expected," he said.
Polish Finance Minister Grzegorz Kolodko said on Friday inflation should fall to between 17.9 percent and 18.2 percent at year-end, but a Reuter poll of 25 banks forecast the figure at 18.7 percent.
Analysts said the uninspiring inflation data were likely to keep demand at a moderate 700 million zlotys against a 1.2 billion offer.
However, analysts said yields were not likely to gain more than a couple of basis points with demand focused on the benchmark 52-week bills.
The paper traded flat near primary average yield levels of 19.50 percent for most of the week in secondary trade.

They said foreign investors were likely to stay sidelined on Monday because of a relatively strong zloty and a decreasing interest rate differential between costs of carry in investment in zlotys (Polish T-bills) and other currencies.
The zloty ended the week flat at 2.8105/15 per dollar and at 1.8652/55 to the mark, or at 2.11/2.08 percent from the trading band centre, against the previous Friday's average 2.10 percent close.

Analysts expected a generally quiet week on the forex market, with some anticipating light currency-selling pressure due to export inflows that have kept the zloty more than two percent from the trading band centre.
"Light currency-selling pressure due to exports inflows is likely to keep the zloty at between 2.1 and 2.2 percent from parity," said Monika Maciolek from BRE SA.
